peoples.s: The largest ethnic group on Earth. Han Chinese make up about 90 percent of China's population and share a written tradition that stretches back more than three thousand years.
peoples.fun: Chinese characters are one of the oldest writing systems still in daily use, with roots in oracle-bone inscriptions about 3,300 years old.
peoples.special: The name Han comes from the Han dynasty (206 BCE to 220 CE), when a shared written culture spread across the empire.

records.text: Largest ethnic group in the world

peoples.s: A people of the Ganges delta known for a rich literary tradition. Bengali is the national language of Bangladesh, and the Language Movement of 1952 is commemorated each year as International Mother Language Day.
peoples.fun: International Mother Language Day, 21 February, honours Bengali speakers who protested for their language in Dhaka in 1952.
peoples.special: Rabindranath Tagore, a Bengali poet, won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature and wrote the words of the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh.

records.text: Tagore was the first non-European winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature

peoples.s: Named for the land of five rivers. Punjabis are among the largest peoples in South Asia and have large communities in Britain, Canada and the Gulf.
peoples.fun: Bhangra, a Punjabi harvest dance, has become a dance style performed around the world.
peoples.special: Langar, the free communal meal served in Sikh gurdwaras, is open to everyone regardless of background.

peoples.home: Tamil Nadu in India, northern Sri Lanka, Singapore
peoples.s: Tamil literature is more than two thousand years old, and Tamil is one of the oldest living classical languages.
peoples.fun: Tamil has a distinctive retroflex sound, written ழ, that few other languages share.
peoples.special: The Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur, completed in 1010 under the Chola dynasty, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

records.text: Tamil is among the oldest living classical languages

peoples.home: Southern and eastern Afghanistan, northwest Pakistan
peoples.s: The largest people in Afghanistan and a very large one in Pakistan. Traditional society is organised around tribes and a code of conduct called Pashtunwali.
peoples.fun: Melmastia, the Pashtun custom of hospitality, obliges a host to feed and protect any guest.
peoples.special: Khushal Khan Khattak, a 17th-century warrior and poet, is celebrated as a national poet of the Pashtuns.

peoples.s: One of the most homogeneous large nations. Japan combines an ancient imperial and Shinto tradition with a highly industrialised modern society.
peoples.fun: Written Japanese mixes three scripts at once: kanji, hiragana and katakana.
peoples.special: Wabi-sabi, an aesthetic that finds beauty in imperfection and impermanence, shapes tea ceremony, ceramics and gardens.

records.text: Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, open since 705, is recognised as the world's oldest hotel

peoples.home: Korean Peninsula, plus communities in China, the US, Japan, Russia
peoples.lang: Korean (a language isolate or Koreanic family)
peoples.s: Koreans share one language and history across two states. The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created in the 15th century under King Sejong.
peoples.fun: Hangul was designed in the 1440s so that ordinary people could learn to read quickly. South Korea celebrates Hangul Day on 9 October.
peoples.special: Kimjang, the making and sharing of kimchi, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in Indonesia. Javanese court culture is known for gamelan orchestras, shadow puppetry and batik cloth.
peoples.fun: Javanese has speech levels, so the words you choose change with the age and status of the person you are speaking to.
peoples.special: Borobudur, a 9th-century Buddhist temple in Central Java, is often described as the largest Buddhist temple in the world.

records.text: Borobudur is often called the largest Buddhist temple in the world

peoples.s: The majority people of Vietnam. Vietnam also recognises 53 other ethnic groups, many living in the highlands.
peoples.fun: Vietnamese is written in Latin letters with accent marks that show its six tones, a system developed with European missionaries in the 1600s.
peoples.special: Tet, the Lunar New Year, is the biggest holiday of the year, when families gather and honour their ancestors.

peoples.s: A traditionally nomadic herding people who built the largest contiguous land empire in history under Genghis Khan in the 13th century.
peoples.fun: The Mongol Empire ran a relay messenger system called the Yam, with stations where riders could swap tired horses for fresh ones.
peoples.special: Naadam, a festival of wrestling, archery and horse racing, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

records.text: The Mongol Empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history

peoples.home: Xinjiang, western China, and Central Asia
peoples.s: A Turkic, mostly Muslim people of the oasis towns along the old Silk Road. Their homeland is in the Xinjiang region of China.
peoples.fun: Uyghur Muqam, a classical musical tradition from Xinjiang, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
peoples.special: Oasis cities such as Kashgar and Turpan were important stops on the Silk Road.

peoples.home: Arabian Peninsula, the Levant, North Africa
peoples.s: A people defined mainly by shared language and culture across 22 countries. Classical Arabic is the language of the Quran and a major medium of science and poetry in the medieval world.
peoples.fun: The word algebra comes from the Arabic al-jabr, the title of a 9th-century book by the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
peoples.special: Scholars at the House of Wisdom in Baghdad translated and built on Greek, Persian and Indian science during the medieval period.

peoples.s: Heirs to the Achaemenid Empire of the 6th century BCE. Persian poetry by writers such as Hafez, Rumi and Ferdowsi is read across the world.
peoples.fun: The Persian Achaemenid Empire built the Royal Road and an early postal relay across its territory.
peoples.special: Nowruz, the Persian New Year, is celebrated at the spring equinox and has been marked for more than 3,000 years.

peoples.home: Turkey, Cyprus, Germany and the Balkans
peoples.s: Turkic peoples migrated from Central Asia into Anatolia from the 11th century. The Ottoman Empire, which lasted until 1922, shaped the modern state.
peoples.fun: Turkish coffee, brewed in a small pot called a cezve, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
peoples.special: The Mevlevi sema, the whirling ceremony associated with the poet Rumi, is also on UNESCO's list.

peoples.home: Israel, the United States, France, Canada, the UK and elsewhere
peoples.lang: Hebrew, plus Yiddish, Ladino and local languages
peoples.s: An ancient people and religious community whose history begins in the Land of Israel. After centuries of dispersion, communities now live on every inhabited continent, and Hebrew is again a spoken national language in Israel.
peoples.fun: Hebrew was revived as an everyday spoken language in modern times, thanks largely to Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and others who worked on it from the 1880s.
peoples.special: Shabbat, a weekly day of rest, has been kept by Jewish communities for thousands of years.
known: Jewish communities developed languages of their own, including Yiddish in Central and Eastern Europe and Ladino among Jews of Spanish origin.
Homeland: Israel, the United States, France, Canada, the UK and elsewhere.

records.text: Hebrew is often described as the only language successfully revived from mainly religious use to a national spoken language

peoples.home: Southeastern Turkey, northern Iraq, Iran, Syria
peoples.s: One of the largest peoples in the world without a state of their own. Their homeland, Kurdistan, spans four countries.
peoples.fun: Newroz, the spring new year, is marked with bonfires and dancing in Kurdish communities.
peoples.special: Kurdish has two major groups of dialects, Kurmanji and Sorani, written in different scripts.

records.text: Among the largest peoples in the world without a state of their own

peoples.home: Armenia, plus Russia, the US, France, Lebanon
peoples.s: Armenia was the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion, in 301 CE. The Armenian alphabet dates to the year 405.
peoples.fun: The oldest known leather shoe, about 5,500 years old, was found in the Areni-1 cave in Armenia.
peoples.special: The Armenian alphabet was created by Mesrop Mashtots in 405 CE and is still used today.

records.text: Armenia was the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion, in 301 CE

peoples.s: Known for the ancient city-states of Ife and Oyo and for bronze and terracotta sculpture. Yoruba religious traditions also shaped practices across the Americas, such as Santería.
peoples.fun: Yoruba is a tonal language, and the talking drum (dundun) imitates the rise and fall of speech.
peoples.special: Ife, a Yoruba city, is known for naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads made centuries ago.

peoples.s: Traditionally organised in village democracies rather than kingdoms. Igbo-Ukwu bronzes date to about the 9th century.
peoples.fun: Bronzes found at Igbo-Ukwu, dated to about the 9th century, show highly advanced lost-wax casting.
peoples.special: The New Yam Festival, Iri ji, marks the harvest with feasting and dancing.

peoples.s: Hausa is a trade language across West Africa. The Hausa city-states, such as Kano, were centres of commerce and Islamic scholarship.
peoples.fun: Hausa was written for centuries in an Arabic-based script called Ajami before the Latin alphabet became common.
peoples.special: Kano, a Hausa city, has been a trading centre for roughly a thousand years, and parts of its old city wall still stand.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in Ethiopia. The traditional Gadaa system organised society into generational grades with elected leaders.
peoples.fun: UNESCO recognised the Gadaa system, in which leaders are chosen by generational grades, as intangible cultural heritage in 2016.
peoples.special: Irreecha, a thanksgiving festival held at the end of the rainy season, draws huge crowds each year.

peoples.s: The largest ethnic group in South Africa. In the early 19th century King Shaka forged the Zulu kingdom into a major regional power.
peoples.fun: Zulu beadwork uses colour combinations that can carry messages between people.
peoples.special: Zulu is the most widely spoken home language in South Africa.

peoples.s: Semi-nomadic cattle herders famous for red shukas, beadwork and the adumu jumping dance.
peoples.fun: A traditional Maasai greeting, Kasserian ingera, means 'And how are the children?'
peoples.special: Maasai have traditionally measured wealth in cattle, and their red shukas are among the most recognisable dress in East Africa.

peoples.home: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, the Sahara
peoples.s: The indigenous people of North Africa, present long before the Arab conquests. The Tuareg of the Sahara are one Amazigh group.
peoples.fun: Tifinagh, an ancient script, is still used to write Tamazight languages, and Yennayer, the Amazigh New Year, falls in mid-January.
peoples.special: Morocco (2011) and Algeria (2016) both recognise Tamazight as an official language.

peoples.s: The largest Slavic people and the biggest ethnic group in Europe. Russian is spoken as a first or second language across much of the former Soviet Union.
peoples.fun: Russian is written in the Cyrillic alphabet, which grew out of work by followers of the missionaries Cyril and Methodius in the 9th century.
peoples.special: The first matryoshka nesting doll was carved in the 1890s.

peoples.s: Germany was a patchwork of states until unification in 1871. Germans have shaped modern philosophy, music and science.
peoples.fun: In German, all nouns are written with a capital letter.
peoples.special: The Brothers Grimm collected folk tales in the early 1800s, preserving stories such as Hansel and Gretel.

peoples.pl: about 5 million in Ireland, many more abroad
peoples.home: Ireland, with large diasporas in the US, UK, Australia
peoples.s: Tens of millions of people worldwide claim Irish ancestry. The Great Famine of the 1840s drove one of the largest emigrations in European history.
peoples.fun: Irish (Gaeilge) is the first official language of the Republic of Ireland and has one of the oldest written traditions in Europe.
peoples.special: St Patrick's Day is celebrated by Irish communities and many others around the world every 17 March.

peoples.home: Basque Country, northern Spain and southwest France
peoples.s: Their language is unrelated to any other living language, and is thought to predate the arrival of Indo-European languages in Europe.
peoples.fun: Euskara, the Basque language, has no known living relatives.
peoples.special: Basque pelota, a handball-like game, is played on special courts called frontons.

records.text: Basque is Europe's best-known language isolate

peoples.home: Northern Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia's Kola Peninsula
peoples.s: The indigenous people of northern Scandinavia. Many Sámi have herded reindeer for centuries.
peoples.fun: Sámi languages have a rich vocabulary for snow, ice and reindeer, reflecting generations of herding.
peoples.special: Joik, a traditional Sámi form of song, expresses a person, animal or place rather than telling a story about it.

peoples.home: Across Europe, especially the Balkans and Central Europe
peoples.s: Language and genetic studies trace the Roma to northern India about a thousand years ago. They are Europe's largest ethnic minority.
peoples.fun: The Romani flag and anthem were adopted at the first World Romani Congress, held near London in 1971. 8 April is International Romani Day.
peoples.special: Romani musicians influenced flamenco in Spain and the brass and string ensembles of Central and Eastern Europe.

peoples.home: The Andes of Peru, Bolivia and Ecuador
peoples.s: Descendants of the Inca and neighbouring peoples. Quechua is spoken today by millions and is an official language in Peru and Bolivia.
peoples.fun: The Inca built the Qhapaq Ñan, a road network of about 30,000 km across the Andes.
peoples.special: The Inca kept records with the quipu, a system of knotted cords.

peoples.s: Builders of Tikal and Chichén Itzá, with a hieroglyphic writing system and an advanced calendar. Maya communities and languages remain very much alive.
peoples.fun: Maya mathematicians used a symbol for zero in their number system.
peoples.special: The Maya used cacao in ceremonial drinks, long before chocolate reached Europe.

peoples.home: Navajo Nation, in Arizona, New Mexico and Utah
peoples.s: The Navajo Nation is the largest reservation in the United States. Navajo code talkers served in the US Marines in World War II.
peoples.fun: During World War II, Navajo code talkers developed a spoken code that was never broken.
peoples.special: Navajo weaving and silversmithing are admired and collected around the world.

records.text: The Navajo Nation is the largest reservation in the United States

peoples.s: Peoples of the Arctic who built a way of life around hunting and the sea ice. Nunavut, in Canada, was created as an Inuit-majority territory in 1999.
peoples.fun: Inuit developed the kayak, a boat built to move quietly while hunting on cold water.
peoples.special: The inuksuk, a stone landmark, helps people find their way and marks good hunting and fishing places.

peoples.s: Polynesian navigators who reached New Zealand around the 13th century. Te reo Māori is an official language of New Zealand.
peoples.fun: The haka, a ceremonial dance with chanting, is used for welcomes, farewells and challenges.
peoples.special: Whakapapa, or genealogy, connects people to their ancestors, to each other and to the land.

records.text: New Zealand was the first self-governing country to give women the vote in national elections, in 1893

peoples.pl: about one million, including Torres Strait Islanders
peoples.s: Among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth, with a presence on the continent for at least 50,000 years.
peoples.fun: The Budj Bim eel traps in Victoria, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are thousands of years old.
peoples.special: Dreaming stories pass on knowledge of law, land and living things through story, song and art.

records.text: Among the oldest continuous living cultures on Earth
